analyst_view.overall: Early view: Celta Fortuna, 16th, have a long injury list (five players named by one report) but should get Joel López, Enrique Ribes and Adrià Capdevila back once their yellow-card bans are served at Albacete. Valladolid have won two in a row under Fran Escribá but are without Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez, and Iván Alejo's fitness after limping off in Gijón is uncertain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already high, and I stay there. Celta Fortuna's games have been open (4-1, 1-5, 2-2 and 1-2 in recent weeks) and Valladolid's last two had seven and three goals, but Valladolid's missing striker Latasa stops me going higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with Valladolid expected to win more than the hosts. That fits a patched-up Celta Fortuna side spending time defending, and I see no news to change it.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: LaLiga's figures show Valladolid with 34 yellows and four reds in 13 games, one of the heavier records in the division, and three Celta Fortuna players have already reached five yellows. Two open sides tend to produce cards in transition.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots and I keep it. Celta Fortuna took 17 at home to Córdoba and Valladolid 15 at Gijón, both consistent with the site's split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Valladolid's attack is without its main striker, and Celta Fortuna's 17 shots against Córdoba brought two goals, so their volume does not always mean accuracy.
